name: Windows — Pass-the-Hash / Overpass-the-Hash Logon Pattern
description:
Attacker objective
Authenticate with a stolen NTLM hash or Kerberos key instead of a password (Pass-the-Hash / Overpass-the-Hash) to impersonate a user.

Attack logic
Tools such as Mimikatz sekurlsa::pth create a logon session with alternate credentials. This produces a distinctive new-credentials (type 9) logon via the seclogo logon process using the Negotiate package — a fingerprint that legitimate runas/network logons do not match.

Why this detection works
Logon auditing (4624) records the logon type, logon process and authentication package; the specific type-9 + seclogo + Negotiate combination isolates the pass-the-hash pattern.

False positives
Some legitimate 'run as different user with network credentials' scenarios; verify the account and process context.

Tuning
Baseline any legitimate tooling that produces this pattern and allowlist it; investigate unexpected occurrences.

Required telemetry
Windows Security 4624 (LogonType, LogonProcessName, AuthenticationPackageName).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Identify the target account and the host; a seclogo type-9 Negotiate logon is the classic pass-the-hash fingerprint.
2. Correlate with the process that initiated it (Mimikatz-style tooling) and the source host.
3. If confirmed, rotate the impersonated account's credentials and treat the host as compromised.
